- **Phase-3 reconciliation.** `UI-CONSOLIDATION-PHASE-3-OP-DETAIL-COMPACT-FIXTURE-CONFORMANCE-R1` is recorded `CLOSED / ACCEPTED` at checkpoint `ded162ec38f30ec7ddf0ab73988fa24bff93967e`. Disclosed and accepted as ruled: the four screenshots were held outside the repository and were **not** independently inspected by the architect; published code and deterministic evidence were accepted. Phase 3's own records are not rewritten.
- **Architecture — one detector, two front-ends.** `scripts/validate-ui-conformance.mjs` plus `scripts/ui-conformance/{contract,inventory,rules}.mjs` and `scripts/ui-conformance/frontends/{dc-html,js-screen}.mjs`. One shared contract reader, one shared rule engine, one prototype front-end, one application front-end, exactly as the canonical plan requires. No helper file beyond the authorized six was created, so no path-boundary amendment was needed. **No new npm dependency**; Node 22.22.3 built-ins only. Filesystem traversal is delegated to the existing `scripts/ui-foundation/inventory.mjs` so the two validators cannot disagree about what exists, and token *classification* is delegated to `scripts/ui-foundation/token-parser.mjs` via `classifyToken` rather than reimplemented.
- **Contract reader — the enums are read, never copied.** The §5 closed-enum JSON block is parsed at run time and the reader fails closed with path and line on invalid JSON, a missing required key, a duplicated §5 block or a missing §5 section. All twelve required keys are validated: `literal_hex_in_screen`, `radius`, `control_h`, `shadow`, `font_size`, `font_weight`, `text_color`, `gap`, `card_padding`, `shell`, `pill_radius_on_button`, `native_select`. The §5 blob hash `f8349e6eeca291fef2edf4d6e30afd628732f00b6495d54eb9273860fa63f1c4` (block at `UI_VISUAL_CONTRACT.md:319`) is carried in every report. Canonical token **values** are resolved from `css/tokens.css` — with cycle guarding and `var()` fallback handling — so `var(--rv-radius)` can be compared against the enum. `--rv-radius-pill`'s value is read from the token, not written into the rule, which is why the detector source contains no `999px`. **Proved, not asserted:** the focused suite rewrites a *temporary* contract's radius enum to `["7px","999px"]` and shows the conforming fixture start failing `UIC-002` while all six detector files stay byte-identical by SHA-256 across the experiment; a second test asserts that no `radius`, `control_h`, `shadow` or `font_size` enum value appears anywhere in detector source.
- **Inventory — 25 of 26 conformance rows resolve to nothing, and that is reported.** The prototype inventory is resolved from the archetype A–F tables of `UI_CONFORMANCE.md`. Exactly **one** row resolves to a tracked file: `docs/ui/fixtures/op-detail-compacto/OP Detail - Compacto.dc.html`. The other **25** name screens that live in the external design project and are reported `NOT_PRESENT_IN_WORKTREE` with their archetype, never silently dropped — a screen the detector cannot open is not a screen the detector has audited. Ambiguous duplicate filenames and duplicate rows for one path are refused the same way. The application inventory is all **66** tracked `js/screens/*.js`. Excluded: `node_modules/**`, `docs/ui/evidence/**`, `docs/ui/fixtures/vendor/**`, `tests/**`, `services/**`, `support.js`, the four chrome/documentation rows, and the `*-standalone.html` / `*-bundle-ready.html` / `*-print-*` derivative pattern.
- **Prototype front-end.** Reads inline `style` **and** `style-hover` attributes and `<style>` rule blocks — the reference fixture uses both, and reading only one would report a clean screen with half its values unexamined. Maintains the element stack, so card membership and in-card containment are facts rather than guesses. HTML comments are blanked with byte offsets preserved, so a colour named in a comment is not read as a screen value while line and column attribution stay exact.
- **Application front-end — it lexes, and it fails rather than guesses.** The screens are classic `window.*` scripts building the DOM through `el(tag, attrs, …)`, so every visual value sits inside a JavaScript string; a text scan would read values out of comments and regular expressions as readily as out of markup. No npm parser is authorized and Node exposes none, so a narrow hand-written lexer classifies comments, strings, template literals and regular-expression literals and nothing more. Regex-versus-division is decided by the preceding significant token, and a `/` in regex position with no same-line terminator is a **hard failure**, not a guess. Decoded style sources: `style:` properties in attribute objects, `.style.prop =`, `.style.cssText =`, `setAttribute('style', …)`, and `style="…"` inside markup string literals. Element role comes from the enclosing `el('tag', {…})` call or from a `x = el('tag'…)` binding. Template substitutions are masked one character per source character, so a `${…}` never shifts a line or column. **No `HARD STOP — JAVASCRIPT SCREEN GRAMMAR REQUIRES AN UNAUTHORIZED PARSER` was reached:** all 66 files lexed completely, 0 `UNSUPPORTED`.
- **Coverage is not a pass — the load-bearing design decision.** Severity has three levels and they are not interchangeable: `blocking` is a contract defect, `debt` is the ratified compatibility block, and `coverage` means the detector **could not decide**. `FULL` means every rule was fully evaluated, not merely that the file parsed. Six constructs degrade a file to `PARTIAL` and each emits an explicit finding: `TEMPLATE_INTERPOLATED_VALUE`, `NON_LITERAL_STYLE_VALUE`, `NON_LITERAL_STYLE_ASSIGNMENT`, `CONCATENATED_STYLE_EXPRESSION`, `CONTROL_ROLE_UNPROVEN`, `CARD_MEMBERSHIP_UNPROVEN`, plus `ACTION_ROW_UNPROVEN` and `PILL_ROLE_UNPROVEN` from the rules. An `UNSUPPORTED` file reports **zero rules evaluated**, never zero defects. During implementation a real instance of the class this guards against was found and fixed: the per-file severity counter and the per-file coverage *state* were both named `coverage`, and the counter silently overwrote the state — exactly the bug that turns "not evaluated" into something a reader mistakes for a verdict. They are now `coverage_gaps` and `coverage`.
- **Rule engine — eleven rules, two of them splits the order required.** `UIC-001` literal colour (`#rgb`, `#rgba`, `#rrggbb`, `#rrggbbaa`, `rgb()`, `rgba()`, `hsl()`, `hsla()`; `currentColor`, `transparent`, `inherit`, `none` legal; `href="#"` never flagged). `UIC-002` radius outside the enum, per component of a multi-value radius, with an unknown token reported as unprovable rather than passed. `UIC-003` control height, scoped to `button`/`input`/`select`/`textarea`, `role="button"`, `data-ui-control` and an anchor dressed as a control — an unrelated geometric height is **not** classified as a control, and an unresolvable role yields a coverage gap instead of silence. `UIC-004` shadow enum plus the cards-are-flat clause, with shadow values that do not resolve through a canonical token reported. `UIC-005` `font-size` and `font-weight`, with `normal`/`bold` mapped. `UIC-006` native `<select>`, detected by both front-ends and by four separate JavaScript forms. `UIC-007` pill radius on a button or button-equivalent — the semantic token, its canonical token value, or any radius at or above the 20px threshold; a pill background does not rescue a pill-shaped button. `UIC-008` card action alignment on explicitly marked `data-card-actions` rows, requiring `flex-end` or `space-between` and, inside a card, the canonical footer divider and `padding-top: 11px`. `UIC-009` deprecated compatibility references, classified by `token-parser.mjs`, summarised per token name, covering both `--rv-color-*` and `--rv-status-*`. `UIC-010` D6.1 semantic-radius scope by element role. `UIC-011` unresolved `var(--rv-*)`. The two splits: an unresolved token is not the same defect as a deprecated one (`UIC-011` vs `UIC-009`), and pill radius on a button is not the same defect as pill radius on a box (`UIC-007` vs `UIC-010`).
- **Table-alignment boundary respected.** Eight tables inventoried; **none** proven and **none** failed automatically. All eight are `MANUAL_REVIEW_REQUIRED`: the fixture's three at lines 140, 168 and 195, three in `js/screens/ordem-compra-receipt-render.js` and two in `js/screens/ordem-compra-render.js`. `AUTOMATICALLY_PROVEN` is emitted only when a `<colgroup>` column count matches the header cell count and `AUTOMATICALLY_FAILED` only when they contradict each other; both branches are pinned by test. The reference fixture's own tables are as unproven as the application's — no pass was fabricated for the reference. Pass 8 remains the manual pass the canonical plan identified.
- **Finding schema and stable order.** Every finding carries `rule_id`, `severity`, `path`, `line`, `column`, `front_end`, `archetype`, `property`, `observed_value`, `resolved_value`, `element_or_context` and `message`. The report carries `detector_version`, `contract_path`, `contract_blob_hash`, `inventory`, `coverage_summary`, `findings`, `summary_by_rule`, `summary_by_file`, `summary_by_archetype`, `deprecated_token_summary`, `table_review_summary`, plus `highlights`. Sort is path, line, column, rule ID, observed value; order is proved stable under reversal and rotation of the input.
- **CLI.** `--report` exits `0` on a successful deterministic scan even with findings; `--enforce` exits `1` when a blocking finding exists; a detector, configuration or inventory failure exits `2`; `--rule <ID>` limits enforcement to one property without hiding any baseline data from the JSON report. (2) **The inventory reader bounds an archetype block at the next *archetype* heading rather than at the next `##` heading of any kind**, so a table of three or more columns whose first cell is a backticked filename is read as rows of the last archetype if it is placed after `## Archetype F`. This was found by this phase's own conformance-state update: writing the new **Application surface** table after archetype F registered all 66 application files a second time as archetype F and doubled the scan to 7 942 findings. It was latent before — the pre-existing post-F chrome table survives only because it has two columns and the reader requires three. The fix is one line, bounding on `^## `, and it is **disclosed, not applied**: `scripts/ui-conformance/inventory.mjs` shipped in this phase's commit 1, the order authorizes exactly two commits and forbids amend, so a third commit or an amend would breach the boundary. Mitigated in the meantime by document layout — § Application surface and § Table review are placed **above** § Archetype A — and by an explicit **Editing rule** section in `UI_CONFORMANCE.md` stating the constraint so it is a stated invariant rather than an accident. **The published baseline is unaffected:** every one of the 3 971 findings and every count was produced with the sections in the layout the file now carries, verified by re-scanning after the layout change and diffing.

So the baseline committed in commit 1 cannot be byte-identical to a scan of commit 2's tree. The delta was measured, not assumed: all **3 971 findings are identical**, prototype count 1 → 1, application count 66 → 66, unresolved names identical, every summary identical, and the **only** difference is the 25 `inventory.unresolved[].line` values, which are line numbers *of the conformance document itself* and shifted because the mandated update inserted sections above the archetype tables. Proved by stripping `line` and comparing the inventories, which are then byte-identical. The committed baseline is therefore the exact evidence for the tree it was generated against, and it remains a faithful record of every finding in the tree at commit 2. `tests/ui-conformance-detector.test.mjs` deliberately does **not** assert the committed baseline against a live scan for this reason; it asserts the contract blob hash, the detector version, the report schema and stable sort order, and proves determinism by comparing two independent detector processes instead.
